subject: Social Media
title: Dark Patterns
description: A short lesson to help you apply Dark Patterns.

hook.text: Unsubscribing takes 12 clicks. Subscribing took one. That asymmetry is designed. It's called a dark pattern.

buildup.text: Dark patterns trick you into actions you didn't intend: sharing data, buying upgrades, staying subscribed.

discovery.text: Harry Brignull named and catalogued dark patterns. Confirmshaming: 'No thanks, I don't want to save money.'

twist.text: Social media uses them constantly. The 'Are you sure you want to leave?' prompt plays on loss aversion.

climax.text: The EU banned the most egregious dark patterns. But subtle ones still fill every platform interface.

punchline.text: If leaving is hard, staying was never your choice.

quiz.question: What are dark patterns in design?
options: Tricks that manipulate users into unintended actions
